title: Consultation Paper on Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Rating Providers for Securities Markets
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Jan 24, 2022'; the embedded PDF (sebi_data/attachdocs/jan-2022/1643027423348.pdf) opens directly from this page and its comment deadline (March 10, 2022) is internally consistent with a Jan 24 issue date.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposes to accredit 'ESG Rating Providers' (ERPs) for the purpose of assigning ESG ratings to listed entities and listed securities; a listed entity availing an ESG rating would have to obtain it only from a SEBI-accredited ERP.
Only SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies (CRAs) and SEBI-registered Research Analysts (RAs) are proposed as entities eligible to be accredited as ERPs.
A minimum net worth of Rs. 10 crore (in addition to the entity's existing CRA/RA net-worth requirement) is proposed as an accreditation condition.
It is proposed that accredited ERPs be mandated to follow a 'subscriber-pay' business model.
content_excerpt: 3.5.1 ... SEBI proposes to accredit ERPs for the purpose of assigning ESG ratings to listed entities and listed securities. 3.5.2. The proposed scope of accreditation of ERPs is as follows: a. A listed entity who intends to avail an ESG rating, shall obtain the same from only a SEBI Accredited ERP. ... 4.2. Proposed eligible entities: In view of above, SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies and SEBI-registered Research Analysts are proposed to be considered eligible to be accredited by SEBI as ERPs, subject to fulfilment of accreditation criteria. ... 5.2. Net worth: ... it is proposed that CRAs/RAs with a minimum net worth of Rs. 10 crores, as per the latest audited financial statements, may be eligible to apply to be a SEBI-accredited ERP. This net worth requirement would be in addition to the applicable minimum net worth requirement for the entity as CRA/RA. ... 11.8. Proposal on Business Model: ... it is proposed that ERPs may be mandated to follow a 'subscriber-pay' business model.

title: Consultation Paper on Regulatory Framework for ESG Rating Providers (ERPs) in Securities Market
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Feb 22, 2023'; PDF filename timestamp (attachdocs/feb-2023/1677081689852.pdf) and the paper's own stated comment deadline (March 8, 2023) are consistent with a Feb 22 issue date.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed that ERPs register with SEBI under a new chapter to be inserted into the SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) Regulations, 1999, rather than through a standalone accreditation scheme.
The paper proposed two registration categories, 'Category I' and 'Category II' ESG Rating Providers, with different net-worth and permitted-services criteria.
It proposed that either an issuer-pays or a subscriber-pays business model be allowed for ERPs (no hybrid), superseding the earlier mandatory subscriber-pay proposal.
It proposed a 'Core ESG Rating' category tied to assured BRSR Core parameters.
content_excerpt: 6. (3) ESG rating provider shall seek registration in one of the categories mentioned hereunder: (a) 'Category I ESG Rating Provider', (b) 'Category II ESG Rating Provider'. ... 16.1 With regard to aforesaid reference to business models of ESG rating providers, it is proposed that either a issuer-pays or a subscriber-pays business model be allowed for ERPs in India. 16.2 However, hybrid business models shall not be allowed for ERPs.

title: Streamlining the Timelines followed in Open Offers and Buyback Tender Offers
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Mar 25, 2022'; PDF (attachdocs/mar-2022/1648209029148.pdf) states a comment deadline of April 15, 2022, consistent with a Mar 25 issue date.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed reducing the overall time for completion of an Open Offer under the Takeover Regulations, 2011 from 62 working days to 42 working days.
SEBI proposed reducing the overall time for completion of a Buyback tender offer under the Buy-back Regulations, 2018 from 43 working days to 36 working days.
Specific proposed changes included shortening the period to publish the Detailed Public Statement (T+5 to T+3) and to submit the Draft Letter of Offer to SEBI (T+10 to T+5).
The Primary Market Advisory Committee (PMAC) had agreed to the proposals, and the Association of Investment Bankers of India (AIBI) welcomed the review.
content_excerpt: 1. The objective of this paper is to seek comments / views from various stakeholders including market intermediaries and the public on procedure followed with respect to the timelines of various activities involved in Open Offers and Buy-back offers... 2. The proposed changes in the timelines of procedural activities would help reduce the overall time taken for completion of Open Offer from 62 working days to 42 working days and overall time for completion of Buyback from 43 working days to 36 working days, which would be investor-friendly and make the process more efficient. ... 6. Primary Market Advisory Committee ('PMAC') agreed to the proposals... 7. AIBI welcomed the proposal regarding review of the timelines of various procedural activities in open offers and buyback tender offers.

title: Consultation Paper on Applicability of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 to Mutual Fund (MF) units
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Jul 08, 2022'; the PDF itself states the comment deadline as 'not later than July 29, 2022 (within 21 calendar days from date of publication)', which is internally consistent with a Jul 8 issue date.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed to cover dealing in units of Mutual Funds under the PIT Regulations by inserting a separate chapter, since MF units were specifically excluded from the definition of 'securities' under the existing PIT Regulations.

The paper proposed definitions of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI), Generally Available Information, Connected Persons, Designated Persons and 'Systematic Transactions' specific to Mutual Funds.

It proposed mandatory disclosure by AMCs of designated persons' MF unit holdings and mandatory reporting of all their MF trades, plus pre-clearance, trading-window-closure and contra-trade restrictions for designated persons.
It proposed a minimum standard code of conduct for designated persons, modeled on the existing Schedule C of the PIT Regulations.
content_excerpt: 1. Objective: ... to solicit public comments / views on the proposal to cover dealing in units of Mutual Funds under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading), Regulations, 2015 ('PIT Regulations') so as to harmonize the regulations governing trading in securities, while in possession of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI)... it is considered to include a separate chapter in PIT Regulations, specifically to cover transactions in the units of Mutual Fund schemes, both close ended and open ended... It is proposed to make AMC disclose the details of holdings in the units of the Mutual Fund... it is proposed to make it mandatory to report all the tradings of Mutual Fund units by designated persons.

title: Consultation Paper on Green and Blue Bonds as a mode of Sustainable Finance
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Aug 04, 2022'; the PDF states comments were due 'latest by August 31, 2022', consistent with an Aug 4 issue date, and a subsequent extension notice (E02) explicitly references this paper's original Aug 2022 publication.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed to amplify the definition of 'green debt securities', including possibly adding 'alternative' instruments such as green revenue bonds, green project bonds and green securitized bonds as defined by ICMA.

SEBI proposed introducing the concept of 'blue bonds' for ocean/marine and water-management projects, and asked whether introducing 'coloured bonds' more broadly (blue bonds for the blue economy, yellow bonds for solar power) would help increase funding channels for green projects.
SEBI sought views on reducing compliance costs for issuers of green debt securities while guarding against 'greenwashing'.
It proposed updating the list of 'eligible' green-bond sectors in line with updated ICMA Green Bond Principles.

Whether the above mentioned initiatives offer any scope for financing through blue bonds? b. Whether introducing coloured bonds (blue bonds for blue economy, yellow bonds for solar power) will help increase channels for funding to green projects?

title: Consultation Paper on Review of disclosure requirements for material events or information under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Nov 12, 2022'; the PDF's own comment deadline is 'no later than November 27, 2022', consistent with a Nov 12 issue date.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed a quantitative materiality threshold: listed entities would have to disclose an event whose value/impact exceeds the lower of 2% of turnover, 2% of net worth, or 5% of the three-year average absolute profit/loss after tax (all per last audited standalone financials).
SEBI proposed reducing the disclosure timeline for material events or information emanating from within the listed entity from twenty-four hours to twelve hours from occurrence.

It proposed that a listed entity's Materiality Policy 'shall not dilute any requirements specified under this regulation' and must help employees escalate potential material events to key managerial personnel.
It proposed detailed event-specific disclosure timelines (12 or 24 hours depending on event type) set out in an annexure.
content_excerpt: 3.1.6. Materiality Threshold: Accordingly, it is proposed that the listed entities shall disclose an event or information specified under Para B whose threshold value or the expected impact in terms of value exceeds the lower of the following: a. two percent of turnover... b. two percent of net worth... c. five percent of three-year average of absolute value of profit/loss after tax... 3.3.3. In order to address the above regulatory concerns, it is proposed that for the material events or information which emanate from the listed entity, the timeline for disclosure by the entity shall be reduced from twenty-four hours to twelve hours.

title: Consultation Paper on Strengthening the Investor Grievance Redressal Mechanism in the Indian Securities Market by harnessing Online Dispute Resolution mechanisms
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Dec 19, 2022'; PDF states comments due 'latest by January 9, 2023', and a subsequent extension notice (E02) confirms the same original deadline.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed making the existing MII-administered mediation/conciliation and arbitration mechanism fully online, end-to-end, using the capacity and technology of ODR institutions.
SEBI proposed extending that modified MII-administered mechanism to cover grievances against all specified securities-market intermediaries, not only MII constituents.

Proposed modifications included relabelling the IGRC process as mediation/conciliation, providing a sole mediator/conciliator/arbitrator irrespective of dispute amount, and doing away with appellate arbitration.
Suggestions were sought on how to fund the resulting grievance redressal mechanism.

The proposed modifications... include relabelling the IGRC process as mediation/conciliation, providing for a sole mediator/conciliator/arbitrator irrespective of the amount of the dispute, and doing away with appellate arbitration.

title: Consultation Paper on Review of Regulatory Framework for Sponsors of a Mutual Fund
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Jan 13, 2023'; the PDF itself is dated 'Issued on: January 13, 2023' with comments due 'no later than January 29, 2023'.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed an 'alternate eligibility route' for entities, including Private Equity funds, that lack the existing 5-year profitability track record, to become MF sponsors, subject to higher net-worth requirements (e.g. AMC net worth of not less than INR 150 crore under one option discussed).
The Working Group recommendation discussed in the paper proposed that Private Equity funds fulfil the alternate eligibility route with additional safeguards.

SEBI proposed a 'Self-Sponsored AMC' concept, under which a mutual fund/AMC meeting specified qualifying conditions could continue operating without a distinct sponsor, holding only 'financial investors' each below a stated stake, letting the original sponsor voluntarily disassociate.

The existing eligibility criteria (positive net worth in preceding 5 years, net worth exceeding capital contribution, profitability in 3 of preceding 5 years or INR 100 crore net worth) were proposed to continue for the existing route.
content_excerpt: A. Objective: The objective of this consultation paper is to seek comments/views from the public on the proposals intending to review the regulatory framework for sponsor(s) of a mutual fund so as to explore the possibility of enabling diverse set of entities, who otherwise may not have been eligible, to be associated with mutual funds with requisite safeguards in place. ... 'Self-Sponsored AMC' ... conditions for becoming a Self-Sponsored AMC may be as under... A mutual fund meeting the qualifying conditions for Self-Sponsored AMC... It can only have 'Financial investors' each holding [a capped stake].

title: Consultation paper on direct plan for schemes of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and trail model for distribution commission in AIFs
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Feb 03, 2023'; the PDF itself sets a comment deadline of 'latest by February 18, 2023', consistent with a Feb 3 issue date.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed mandating AIFs to offer a 'Direct Plan' entailing no distribution/placement fee, and that investors approaching an AIF through an intermediary separately charging a fee (e.g. advisory or portfolio-management fee) be onboarded via the direct plan only.
SEBI proposed that Category III AIF investors be charged placement/distribution fee purely on a trail basis (no upfront).
SEBI proposed that Category I and II AIF investors be charged on a trail basis too, but with up to one-third of the present value of total distribution fee payable upfront in the first year.
The proposals originated from AIPAC (the SEBI Alternative Investment Policy Advisory Committee), which deliberated and recommended both changes.
content_excerpt: 4.4. AIFs to be mandated to offer the option of a Direct Plan for investors, entailing no distribution/ placement fee. 4.5. AIFs to ensure that any investor approaching an AIF through an intermediary, that is separately charging the investor a fee..., invests in the AIF via the direct plan route only. ... 5.7. In case of Category III AIFs, investors may be charged placement fee/distribution fee on a trail basis. In case of Category I AIFs and Category II AIFs, investors may also be charged on trail basis, however, certain higher amount of placement/distribution fee (viz: one-third of the present value of the total distribution fee) may be paid upfront in the first year.

title: Consultation paper on Investor consent for buying/selling investments from/to associates of AIFs
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Feb 03, 2023'; PDF is dated 'Issued on: February 03, 2023' with comments due 'latest by February 18, 2023'.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed that 'An AIF shall not buy or sell investments, except with the approval of 75% of investors by value of their investment in the AIF, from or to (a) associates; or (b) schemes of AIFs managed or sponsored by its Manager, Sponsor or their associates.'
The Alternative Investment Policy Advisory Committee (AIPAC), at its January 20, 2023 meeting, had already in-principle agreed to this 75%-investor-approval mechanism.

The stated rationale was to address conflict-of-interest concerns in AIF dealings with associates, extending an existing investor-consent requirement that previously applied only to investments in associates, not to buying/selling to/from them.
content_excerpt: 4. Proposal: Taking into account the recommendations of AIPAC, the following is proposed: 'An AIF shall not buy or sell investments, except with the approval of 75% of investors by value of their investment in the AIF, from or to a) associates; or b) schemes of AIFs managed or sponsored by its Manager, Sponsor or their associates.'

title: Consultation paper on proposal for introduction of the concept of General Information Document (GID) and Key Information Document (KID), mandatory listing of debt securities of listed issuers and other reforms under the NCS Regulations
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Feb 09, 2023'; the PDF states comments due 'latest by February 24, 2023 (within 15 days from date of publication)', consistent with a Feb 9 issue date.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed introducing a General Information Document (GID), valid for one year, to replace repeated placement memoranda for issuers making multiple non-convertible-securities issuances in a year, plus a shorter Key Information Document (KID) for each subsequent issuance.

SEBI proposed parity between initial disclosures in a prospectus for public issuance of debt securities/NCRPS and a placement memorandum for private placement of non-convertible securities proposed to be listed.

SEBI proposed that issuers with already-listed debt securities be required to make all future debt issuances in listed form (mandatory listing), noting this would not add compliance burden since such issuers already comply with LODR continuous-disclosure conditions.
The paper proposed other definitional/procedural reforms under the NCS Regulations, 2021.

Parity betwen initial disclosures required to be made in a prospectus for public isuance of debt securities/ NCRPS and a placement memorandum for private placement of non-convertible securities proposed to be listed... 3.4.1. The proposal is aimed at isuers having listed debt securities who are already required to comply with the continuous listing conditions including disclosure requirements under the LODR regulations. Therefore, the proposed mandate of making al future isuances in listed category would not create aditional compliance burden on the isuer.

title: Consultation Paper on certain Amendments to Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, with the objective of increasing transparency and streamlining certain processes
date_verification: SEBI listing page date field reads 'Feb 22, 2023'; PDF sets a comment deadline of 'no later than March 08, 2023', consistent with a Feb 22 issue date.
extracted_claims: SEBI proposed that if underwriting for shortfall in demand or subscription risk is opted by the issuer in a public issue, this must be disclosed in the offer document prior to issue opening.

SEBI proposed that a listed entity may announce a bonus issue only after obtaining stock-exchange approval for listing/trading of all its pre-bonus securities, and that bonus issues be made only in dematerialised form.
